bio-hl.topic: Linking questions: unity and diversity (theme A)

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is the correct order of increasing level of organisation?
questions.hint: Start with the smallest unit.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which feature is shared by ALL living cells (unity)?
questions.hint: Prokaryotes lack a nucleus, animals lack walls.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: The universality of the genetic code is evidence for…
questions.hint: If every organism reads codons the same way…

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which molecule is the universal energy currency in cells?
questions.hint: It has three phosphate groups.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Water's high specific heat capacity helps organisms because it…
options: makes water less dense when frozen
questions.hint: Think of thermal stability.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is an example of DIVERSITY arising at the molecular level?
options: different amino acid sequences giving different protein shapes
all DNA having a double helix
questions.answer: different amino acid sequences giving different protein shapes
questions.hint: Same building blocks, different arrangements.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells both contain…
questions.hint: Protein synthesis happens in all cells.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: The ribosomes of prokaryotes are…
questions.hint: They are smaller than eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosomes.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: The presence of 70S ribosomes and circular DNA in mitochondria supports…
questions.hint: These organelles resemble bacteria.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement links unity and diversity in classification?
options: Organisms share features with common ancestors yet differ due to evolution
All organisms in a genus are identical
questions.answer: Organisms share features with common ancestors yet differ due to evolution
questions.hint: Evolution explains both.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A linking question differs from a standard question because it…
options: requires connecting ideas from more than one topic
questions.answer: requires connecting ideas from more than one topic
questions.hint: 'Linking' is the clue.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the process by which new species form from existing ones.
questions.hint: It's how diversity of species increases.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is a property that emerges at the level of an organism but not of a single molecule?
questions.hint: Emergent properties arise from interactions of many parts.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which HL concept explains how a single genome produces diverse cell types in one organism?
questions.hint: Cells switch different genes on and off.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Discuss how epigenetic changes and gene regulation link molecular processes to diversity of cells and organisms. Use at least two examples.
questions.hint: Think of methylation, histone modification and cell differentiation.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Using examples from at least two levels of organisation, explain how the structure of a molecule relates to its function in a cell.
questions.hint: Consider a protein such as an enzyme or a membrane component.

bus-hl.topic: Paper 1 pre-released statement: researching the context

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In IB Business Management, the Paper 1 pre-released statement is released…
options: about four months before the exam
on the morning of the exam
questions.answer: about four months before the exam
questions.hint: It gives time for research before the exam.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What does the pre-released statement mainly provide?
options: the context, setting and organisation for the case study
questions.answer: the context, setting and organisation for the case study
questions.hint: Questions are unseen; context is known.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: The best first step when you receive the pre-released statement is to…
options: read it closely and identify the organisation, industry and key issues
questions.answer: read it closely and identify the organisation, industry and key issues
questions.hint: Understand before you research.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the business term for a set of firms producing similar products, e.g. all fast-food chains?
questions.hint: It's the wider sector the case organisation belongs to.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which tool helps analyse the external environment of an industry?
questions.hint: It covers social, technological, economic, environmental… factors.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Why build a glossary while researching the statement?
options: to use precise business terminology accurately in answers
to copy definitions into every answer word for word
questions.answer: to use precise business terminology accurately in answers
questions.hint: Examiners reward correct terms applied to context.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: 'Application' in IB Business answers means…
options: linking theory to the specific case organisation
questions.answer: linking theory to the specific case organisation
questions.hint: Use the case's facts.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which source is MOST useful for researching an unfamiliar industry?
options: reputable industry reports and news articles
questions.answer: reputable industry reports and news articles
questions.hint: Look for reliable, current information.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A key risk of over-researching a real company similar to the case is…
options: using facts that contradict the fictional case
questions.answer: using facts that contradict the fictional case
questions.hint: The case organisation is the authority in the exam.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which analysis lists a firm's Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats?
questions.hint: Four letters.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In a SWOT analysis, a new competitor entering the market is a(n)…
questions.hint: It is external and negative.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is an INTERNAL factor?
questions.hint: Internal factors are within the firm's control.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain two ways researching the industry context could improve your Paper 1 answers.
questions.hint: Think of application and evaluation.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Outline a plan (3–5 steps) for preparing for Paper 1 using the pre-released statement.
questions.hint: Include reading, research, glossary and practice.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which command term requires a balanced review with a conclusion?
questions.hint: It weighs strengths and limitations.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: HL: Discuss how understanding the ethical and environmental issues in an industry could help you answer a strategic question about the case organisation.
questions.hint: Link CSR, stakeholder interests and long-term strategy.

chem-hl.topic: Synthesis: particles, atoms and the mole (Structure 1)

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which subatomic particle determines the identity of an element?
questions.hint: Atomic number counts these.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of ³⁷Cl (Z = 17)?
questions.hint: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Line spectra provide evidence that electrons in atoms…
questions.hint: Only specific wavelengths are emitted.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In the hydrogen emission spectrum, the lines converge at…
questions.hint: Energy levels get closer together further from the nucleus.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across period 3?
options: nuclear charge increases while shielding stays similar
electrons are added to new shells
questions.answer: nuclear charge increases while shielding stays similar
questions.hint: More protons, same shell.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Write the full electron configuration of sodium (Z = 11).
questions.hint: Fill 1s, 2s, 2p, then 3s.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the number of moles in 9.00 g of water (M = 18.02 g/mol). Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: n = m / M.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What mass of CO₂ (M = 44.01 g/mol) is produced when 0.250 mol of carbon burns completely? Give your answer to 3 significant figures, in grams.
questions.hint: C + O₂ → CO₂ is 1:1.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: How many molecules are in 0.500 mol of a gas? (L = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹) Give your answer in the form a × 10^b, entering only a with b = 23.
questions.hint: N = n × L.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A gas occupies 2.27 dm³ at STP (molar volume 22.7 dm³ mol⁻¹). How many moles is this?
questions.hint: n = V / Vm.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: 2.00 g of NaOH (M = 40.00 g/mol) is dissolved to make 250 cm³ of solution. What is the concentration in mol dm⁻³?
questions.hint: Convert cm³ to dm³ first.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The empirical formula of a compound that is 40.0% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass is…
questions.hint: Divide each % by its atomic mass, then by the smallest.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, how many moles of NH₃ form from 6.0 mol of H₂ (excess N₂)?
questions.hint: Use the mole ratio 3 : 2.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which linking idea connects electron configuration to periodicity?
options: Elements in the same group have the same outer electron configuration
All elements have the same number of shells
questions.answer: Elements in the same group have the same outer electron configuration
questions.hint: Group behaviour comes from valence electrons.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: HL: Successive ionisation energies of an element show a large jump between the 3rd and 4th. The element is most likely in group…
questions.hint: The jump appears after removing all valence electrons.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: HL: Explain why the first ionisation energy of aluminium is lower than that of magnesium.
questions.hint: Compare the sub-level of the electron removed (3p vs 3s).

comp-hl.topic: Theme A practice: computer fundamentals and networks

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which component carries out arithmetic and logic operations in the CPU?
questions.hint: Arithmetic Logic Unit.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.hint: It 'counts' through the program.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which type of memory is volatile?
questions.hint: It loses its contents when power is off.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Cache memory improves performance because it…
options: stores frequently used data close to the CPU
questions.answer: stores frequently used data close to the CPU
questions.hint: Speed and proximity.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the output of NOT(A AND B) when A = 1 and B = 1? (0 or 1)
questions.hint: AND first, then invert.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which logic gate outputs 1 only when its inputs differ?
questions.hint: Exclusive OR.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which is a function of an operating system?
questions.hint: The OS manages resources.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the binary number 101101 to denary.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A LAN differs from a WAN because a LAN…
questions.hint: Local Area Network.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which device forwards data packets between different networks?
questions.hint: It routes between networks.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which protocol is used to translate domain names into IP addresses?
questions.hint: Domain Name System.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In packet switching, packets of one message…
options: may take different routes and are reassembled at the destination
always travel along one fixed circuit
questions.answer: may take different routes and are reassembled at the destination
questions.hint: Each packet has a sequence number.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which measure protects data in transit from being read if intercepted?
questions.hint: It scrambles data with a key.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A firewall's main purpose is to…
options: filter incoming and outgoing network traffic using rules
questions.answer: filter incoming and outgoing network traffic using rules
questions.hint: Think of a barrier with rules.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain the difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption.
questions.hint: Think of how many keys are used and how they are shared.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe the stages of the fetch–decode–execute cycle, using precise register names.
questions.hint: Mention PC, MAR, MDR and CIR.

comp-sl.topic: Theme A practice: computer fundamentals and networks

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which component of the CPU performs arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.hint: Think of the unit named after the operations it carries out.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.hint: It 'counts' through the program.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which type of primary memory is volatile?
questions.hint: Volatile memory loses its contents when power is removed.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: State the term for small, very fast memory located on or near the CPU that stores frequently used data.
questions.hint: It sits between the registers and RAM in the memory hierarchy.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the output of an XOR gate when both inputs are 1?
questions.hint: XOR is true only when the inputs differ.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which Boolean expression is equivalent to NOT (A AND B)?
questions.hint: Apply De Morgan's law.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of the following is a function of an operating system?
options: Compiling source code into a web page
questions.hint: Think of resources the OS allocates between programs.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: State the term for the OS technique that uses secondary storage as an extension of RAM.
questions.hint: Pages are swapped between RAM and disk.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which network type typically covers a single building or campus?
questions.hint: The L stands for a small area.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: At which layer of the OSI model does IP addressing operate?
questions.hint: Routing between networks happens at this layer.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which protocol provides reliable, connection-oriented delivery of data?
questions.hint: It uses acknowledgements and retransmission.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: State the name of the device that forwards data packets between different networks.
questions.hint: It reads IP addresses to choose a path.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which security measure converts plaintext into ciphertext?
questions.hint: Only someone with the key can read the result.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A user receives a fake email asking them to enter their password on a lookalike website. This is an example of:
questions.hint: It relies on tricking the user, not on breaking the system.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe two differences between a VPN and a standard public internet connection.
questions.hint: Think about encryption and the 'tunnel' through which data travels.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why packet switching makes efficient use of network bandwidth.
questions.hint: Consider how packets from many users share the same links and can take different routes.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Import substitution industrialisation (ISI) aims mainly to:
options: Replace imported manufactured goods with domestic production
questions.answer: Replace imported manufactured goods with domestic production
questions.hint: The name describes the strategy.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which policy tool is most closely associated with ISI?
questions.hint: ISI protects infant industries from foreign competition.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: State the argument used to justify protecting new domestic firms until they can achieve economies of scale.
questions.hint: Think of the 'age' of the firms being protected.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Export promotion focuses on:
options: Producing goods for which the country has a comparative advantage for world markets
Producing only for the domestic market
questions.answer: Producing goods for which the country has a comparative advantage for world markets
questions.hint: Growth is driven by selling abroad.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which of the following is a common criticism of ISI?
options: It always leads to large trade surpluses
questions.hint: Consider the effect of having no foreign competition.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Many Latin American economies used ISI most widely in which period?
questions.hint: It was popular in the post-war decades, before the debt crisis of the 1980s.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which event in the 1980s led many Latin American countries to move away from ISI?
options: The end of the gold rush
questions.hint: It is often called the 'lost decade'.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: State the term for a country spreading its production and exports across a wider range of goods and services.
questions.hint: It reduces the risk of relying on one commodity.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Over-dependence on primary commodity exports exposes an economy mainly to:
questions.hint: Commodity prices rise and fall sharply.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: The Prebisch–Singer hypothesis suggests that, over the long run, the terms of trade of primary commodity exporters tend to:
questions.hint: Compare the income elasticity of demand for primary vs manufactured goods.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Fair trade schemes typically guarantee producers:
options: A minimum price for their product
questions.answer: A minimum price for their product
questions.hint: It protects farmers when world prices fall.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which is a limitation of fair trade as a development strategy?
options: It covers only a small share of world trade
It always raises world prices for all producers
It removes the need for certification
It bans exports to rich countries
questions.answer: It covers only a small share of world trade
questions.hint: Think about its scale relative to total exports.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain how export promotion can contribute to economic growth in a developing country.
questions.hint: Link exports to aggregate demand, economies of scale and foreign exchange earnings.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Evaluate the use of import substitution as a strategy for economic development.
questions.hint: Weigh protection of infant industries and jobs against inefficiency, higher prices and limited markets.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Using a Latin American example of your choice, discuss the advantages and disadvantages of relying on commodity exports.
questions.hint: Consider price volatility, Dutch disease and the potential for diversification.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Discuss whether diversification is more effective than fair trade in reducing poverty in developing economies.
questions.hint: Compare the scale and long-term effects of each approach; reach a reasoned judgement.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which strategy encourages a country to produce manufactured goods at home instead of buying them from abroad?
questions.hint: Imports are 'substituted' by local goods.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A government places a tariff on imported cars to help a new local car industry grow. This is an example of:
questions.hint: The policy protects domestic production from imports.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Give the abbreviation for import substitution industrialisation.
questions.hint: Use the first letter of each word.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which is an example of an export promotion policy?
options: Raising import quotas on all goods
questions.hint: These zones attract firms that produce for world markets.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Export-led growth relies mainly on increasing:
questions.hint: Exports are an injection into the circular flow.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: One advantage of export promotion is that it can:
questions.hint: Exports bring in foreign currency.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: One disadvantage of ISI is that:
questions.hint: Protected domestic firms face less pressure to cut costs.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: State the term for when a country relies on producing and exporting a wide variety of goods rather than one main product.
questions.hint: The opposite of relying on a single commodity.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Why can dependence on a single commodity be risky?
options: Its price can fall sharply on world markets
It always leads to inflation of zero
questions.answer: Its price can fall sharply on world markets
questions.hint: Think about what happens to export earnings when prices fall.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which of these is a primary commodity?
questions.hint: Primary goods come directly from natural resources.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What does fair trade certification aim to provide for small producers?
options: A minimum price and a social premium
Higher import tariffs in their own country
questions.answer: A minimum price and a social premium
questions.hint: The premium is often invested in the community.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which statement about fair trade is correct?
options: It accounts for a small share of global trade
It only applies to manufactured goods
questions.answer: It accounts for a small share of global trade
questions.hint: Think about how often you see the label compared with other products.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: In the 1980s, many Latin American countries faced a crisis linked to large foreign loans. State the name of this crisis.
questions.hint: It was caused by borrowing that became hard to repay.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of import substitution for a developing country.
questions.hint: Think about jobs in new industries and the effect of protection on efficiency or prices.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain why diversification can make a developing economy less vulnerable to external shocks.
questions.hint: Consider what happens if the price of one export suddenly falls.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Evaluate fair trade as a way of improving the incomes of small farmers.
questions.hint: Consider who benefits, certification costs and the scale of fair trade markets.

en-hl.topic: Paper 2 essay structures: point-by-point and block

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In a point-by-point comparative essay, each body paragraph usually:
options: Discusses both texts in relation to one idea
Summarises the plot of one text
questions.answer: Discusses both texts in relation to one idea
questions.hint: The comparison happens inside every paragraph.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In a block structure, the writer:
options: Discusses one text fully, then the other
Alternates between texts sentence by sentence
Writes only an introduction and conclusion
questions.answer: Discusses one text fully, then the other
questions.hint: Each text gets its own 'block'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which essay structure (point-by-point or block) is generally considered better at keeping comparison sustained throughout the essay?
questions.hint: Think about where the comparison happens in each paragraph.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the main risk of using a block structure in Paper 2?
options: The essay becomes two separate analyses
questions.answer: The essay becomes two separate analyses
questions.hint: Examiners reward comparison and contrast.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: If you use a block structure, how can you make it more comparative?
options: Refer back to the first text explicitly in the second block
Avoid mentioning the first text again
Write the blocks in different languages
questions.answer: Refer back to the first text explicitly in the second block
questions.hint: Use linking phrases that look back.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which connective best signals contrast between two works?
questions.hint: Look for the word that introduces a difference.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which connective best signals similarity?
questions.hint: It means 'in the same way'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What should a thesis in a Paper 2 essay do?
options: Make a clear comparative argument answering the question
questions.answer: Make a clear comparative argument answering the question
questions.hint: It answers the question and links both works.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In a PEEL paragraph, what does the second E usually stand for?
questions.hint: P–E–E–L: point, evidence, ..., link.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which topic sentence is most suitable for a point-by-point paragraph?
options: Both works use setting to reflect the protagonists' isolation, though in contrasting ways.
The first novel is set in a village.
This essay will talk about two books.
I liked the second work more.
questions.answer: Both works use setting to reflect the protagonists' isolation, though in contrasting ways.
questions.hint: It should name a shared focus and hint at comparison.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A question asks how two works present conflict between generations. A good point-by-point plan would organise paragraphs by:
options: Aspects of the conflict, such as causes, language and resolution
Chapter numbers of the first work
questions.answer: Aspects of the conflict, such as causes, language and resolution
questions.hint: Each paragraph tackles one aspect across both works.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which criterion in Paper 2 focuses on how well the essay is organised and how ideas are connected?
questions.hint: Think of the criterion about structure.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain when a block structure might be a sensible choice for a Paper 2 essay.
questions.hint: Consider questions where the works are very different, or where a staged argument helps.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write a topic sentence and a linking sentence for a point-by-point paragraph comparing how two works use symbolism.
questions.hint: The topic sentence should name both works' use of a symbol; the link should return to the question.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A hybrid structure in a comparative essay usually means:
options: Mixing point-by-point paragraphs with short focused sections on each work
Writing half the essay in note form
Comparing three works instead of two
questions.answer: Mixing point-by-point paragraphs with short focused sections on each work
questions.hint: It combines features of both structures.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of point-by-point and block structures for a question on the representation of power in two works.
questions.hint: Weigh sustained comparison against depth of analysis, and reach a judgement.

options: Early in the body, or built up to near the end

questions.hint: It is a comparative essay.

options: Works studied in the course that were not used for Paper 1
Unseen texts given in the exam
questions.answer: Works studied in the course that were not used for Paper 1
questions.hint: Think about which works you bring to the exam.

questions.q: Paper 2 questions are generally:
options: General and conceptual, not about specific works
questions.answer: General and conceptual, not about specific works
questions.hint: They must apply to many possible works.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: State the type of essay required in Paper 2 (one word).
questions.hint: You must discuss similarities and differences.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A question like 'Discuss how two works present a character who changes' focuses mainly on:
questions.hint: Look at the key noun.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A question like 'How do two works use time and its passing?' focuses mainly on:
questions.hint: Time is often shaped through structure.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: When choosing works for a question, the most important factor is:
options: Whether both works offer rich, comparable material for the question
Which work you read most recently
questions.answer: Whether both works offer rich, comparable material for the question
questions.hint: You need enough to compare in depth.

questions.subject: en_lit

questions.answer: Identify the key terms and what the question really asks
questions.hint: Underline the focus words.

options: A thesis, paragraph topics and key evidence from both works
The plot of each work in detail
questions.answer: A thesis, paragraph topics and key evidence from both works
questions.hint: Think about what keeps the essay focused.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In the exam there are no texts provided, so supporting references to the works must come from your _____. (one word)
questions.hint: You need to prepare quotations in advance.

questions.hint: Think about effects on the audience.

questions.q: Explain how you would decide which two works to use for a question about the presentation of a community.

geog-hl.topic: Paper 2 Section B: infographic and visual stimulus analysis

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: When describing a trend in an infographic, you should first:
options: State the overall pattern, then support it with data
questions.answer: State the overall pattern, then support it with data
questions.hint: Describe before you explain.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which command term requires you to give a detailed account of a pattern without explaining why?
questions.hint: It is about 'what', not 'why'.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which command term requires reasons or causes?
questions.hint: Look for the word that asks 'why'.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A good description of data in a Paper 2 answer should include:
options: Only the title of the infographic
questions.hint: Quantify your answer.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: An infographic shows that urban population in a country rose from 40 million to 50 million. Calculate the percentage increase.
questions.hint: Change ÷ original × 100.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A graph shows CO₂ emissions of 8 tonnes per person in Country A and 2 tonnes per person in Country B. How many times higher is A than B?
questions.hint: Divide the larger value by the smaller.

questions.subject: geog

questions.hint: Distinguish percentage points from percentage change.

questions.subject: geog

questions.hint: Change ÷ original × 100.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which feature of an infographic should you check before interpreting the data?
questions.hint: A misleading axis can change your reading.

questions.subject: geog

options: There is a correlation, but not necessarily causation
questions.answer: There is a correlation, but not necessarily causation
questions.hint: Be careful about cause and effect.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A data value that is very different from the general pattern is called:
questions.hint: Mention these in your description.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Name the type of map that uses shading of areas to show different values of a variable.
questions.hint: Darker shading usually means a higher value.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: To link an infographic about migration to a core concept, which term would be most relevant?
questions.hint: Think about why people move.

questions.subject: geog

questions.answer: High birth rates and a youthful population
questions.hint: The base shows the youngest age groups.

questions.subject: geog

questions.hint: Think about trade, dependency, power and global interactions.

questions.subject: geog

questions.hint: Consider source, date, scale, missing data and simplification.
